title: Measured leaves kept under view retention, and every VirtualList kind on scroll layers: horizontal, sticky, SynchronizedOffset and ParentViewport lists composite, RayX's parent-viewport invalidation narrowed, timings measured

New group: horizontal composite counters over 60 frames; the horizontal case moved out of `ineligible`.
New group: horizontal quads at 1 and 1.25 and random histories.

New group: a ParentViewport list keeps its parent's layer; metrics, range and frames per frame against layers off.
New RayX group: ListView and TreeView in ParentViewport keep the parent layer and do not rebuild their state view.
Existing ParentViewport consumer tests, selected on purpose: the proof that narrowing the dependent registration preserves programmatic scroll and mutation behaviour.
New RayX group: sticky ListView, horizontal ListView, sticky TreeView and DataTable synchronized rows composite.
The four TM-1 scenarios' attribution tests (named `scroll_virtual_list*`).
Lane G timing of the fast-mode suite on the owner's Mac (display awake); the report is read and recorded by hand.
The whole `fast::` lib suite (left to CI).

New group: uniform_list's measured item is kept on scroll-only frames, with layers and with view retention alone, and measured again when it changes.
Lane C's scroll-layer suites in full mode, narrowed to those groups (the validation rules: a change to snapping runs --full before it is called proved).
The parent-viewport scenario's attribution test.
This epic's and gpux-virtual-list's lib groups after the merge.

sprints.title: A ParentViewport list keeps its parent's layer

tasks.title: Paint the painted region, answer metrics and range on composited frames
Narrow RayX's dependent-view registration for ParentViewport
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement d-parent-viewport-promotion's RayX side in ListViewState and TreeState, plus the `parent_viewport_layers` group. The existing ParentViewport tests must keep passing.

Commit in RayX paired with t06's gpux commit. The superseded RayX decision is promoted after the epic: do not edit memory now.

Outcome (2026-10-18): ListViewState no longer registers as a dependent view of a `ParentViewport` parent handle under view retention; TreeState never registered. The group's range recorder subscribes from an entity of its own: a subscriber on the view holding the `div` is updated by every range event, a real change of that view.

tasks.title: Keep a row-renderer change visible under fast mode
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
The owner decided (2026-10-18), relayed by the coordinating session, first: "take (B), and fix the TreeView bug in the same sprint": (B) was a gpux rule under which writes an owner makes while it renders only because a scroll notified it count as repeats; the TreeView bug was TreeBase's `set_render_item` write taken to be never stamped. Implementing them showed both rest on a misdiagnosis. ListView demoted the parent's layer because the test's own `VisibleRangeChanged` subscriber lived on the view holding the `div`, which every range event updated, a real change of that view; with the subscriber on an entity of its own and ListViewState's dependent registration narrowed, ListView keeps the layer with or without (B), as composited frames keep the div's content and never lay out its children. TreeBase's write is stamped: it never showed because those frames skip the layout that runs it, so the TreeView bug does not exist. The owner then decided: "revert (B), keep the new regression tests, and record your decision and this outcome in the epic". (B) and the TreeView fix are withdrawn; `row_renderer_changes` stays as regression coverage. A parent that subscribes to the list's events is still a real change on every range change, so the list's state view is built again then; that limit is with the owner.

Add the RayX regression group `row_renderer_changes`, in RayX's t07 commit's pairing, its own commit.

tasks.title: Write a collection's state only when it changes
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
For the row renderer's sameness the owner chose (2026-10-18): "Yes, A + B together": (A) the write is skipped when the scroll policy and scrollbar are unchanged and the row renderer is provably the same, of the same type and capture-free (zero-sized); a capturing closure still writes, as before. (B) an opt-in `renderer_key(k)` (Eq) on `list_view(..)` and on TreeBase: an equal key skips the write; without a key, behaviour stays as before.

Implement d-conditional-state-writes in ListView's and TreeBase's elements and extend `row_renderer_changes`.
